provisions.title: H.J. Res. 39
provisions.heading: Congressional disapproval of the identified FTC premerger-notification reporting and waiting-period rule
provisions.quote: That Congress disapproves the rule submitted by the Federal Trade Commission relating to Premerger Notification; Reporting and Waiting Period Requirements (89 Fed. Reg. 89216; published November 12, 2024), and such rule shall have no force or effect.
provisions.context:
H.J. Res. 39 invokes chapter 8 of title 5 and identifies one Federal Trade Commission rule by title, Federal Register citation, and publication date. Mr. Fitzgerald, for himself, Mr. Gooden, and Mr. Cline, submitted the analyzed introduced-in-House version on February 11, 2025, and it was referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary. Congress.gov separately records no later action. Its sole operative clause states that Congress disapproves the cited rule and that the rule shall have no force or effect; because the resolution remains introduced rather than enacted, that legal consequence remains contingent on enactment.

Source limits / honesty note: The cited rule is not reproduced, and the resolution supplies no findings, substantive replacement rule, implementation steps, quantitative target, reporting requirement, or downstream outcome. The source therefore supports only the express legal objective and enactment-contingent legal effect recorded below. It does not support a claim about premerger filings, review timing, merger activity, competition, compliance costs, or FTC workload. The binary legal consequence is not a recurring empirical series, so this provision honestly has no forecastable metrics, series hints, stance matrices, or conditionals.
goals: Disapprove the Federal Trade Commission rule cited at 89 Fed. Reg. 89216 so that it has no force or effect.

effects.mechanism: Direct legal effect — conditional on enactment
effects.text: If enacted, the resolution would disapprove the identified Federal Trade Commission rule and provide that it has no force or effect; the text does not state what regulatory status would replace it or identify any downstream outcome.
